effective.basis: Per-card ruling chronology from two archived official documents: the UDE Card Rulings capture of 2005-06-16 expressly permits activation with no "Buster Blader" in hand, Deck or Graveyard subject to verification (the effect then disappearing); Konami's yugioh-card.com Card FAQ capture of 2008-12-15 expressly forbids activation in that case.

corroboration.quote: If there is no "Buster Blader" in your hand/Deck/Graveyard you can still activate this effect but your opponent can verify the contents to make certain, and then the effect disappears.
If there are no "Buster Blader" in your hand, Deck, and Graveyard, you cannot activate "Skilled White Magician's" effect that Special Summons "Buster Blader".

changes.historical_text: Each time you or your opponent activates 1 Spell Card, put 1 Spell Counter on this card (max. 3). Tribute this card with 3 Spell Counters on it to Special Summon 1 "Buster Blader" from your hand, Deck, or Graveyard.
changes.summary: Period procedure plus a per-card activation ruling, not a text erratum: the GOAT script reduces s.sptg to the free-zone test alone (the modern Duel.IsExistingMatchingCard over Deck, hand and Graveyard is removed), so the 3-Spell-Counter Tribute effect can be activated with no "Buster Blader" anywhere, and it proves the failure by revealing hand and Deck (Duel.GoatConfirm(tp,LOCATION_HAND+LOCATION_DECK); the Graveyard is already public); the modern script requires an available "Buster Blader" to activate and never reveals. Period rulings add that in the old era the effect simply disappeared on resolution.

review.notes: Chain starts at v1 (DR1-EN119, 2005-03-19), the text the GOAT variant carries exactly; v0 (MFC-064) predates it and states the same Main Phase Tribute in older phrasing. v1->v2 (TP7-EN013) ->v3 (BP01-EN131) ->v4 (SBCB-EN007) ->v5 (SBC1-ENA07) are cosmetic: 'when that Spell resolves' prints the ruling already in force in 2005, and both scripts place the counter in the resolution handler. Dated exactly like its Skilled Dark Magician twin, from the two archived captures rather than the shared 'search-verification' chronology, because this card's fail-to-find allowance ended before the general verification procedure did: GOAT (2005-04-01) takes the historical implementation, Edison (2010-04-24) takes the modern card. Residual not modelled as a version: a chain-forced whiff after 2008-12-15 would presumably still have been verifiable until the general procedure ended; no upstream implementation exists for that intermediate state and it has no practical effect. Remaining diff hunks (re:IsActiveType(TYPE_SPELL) vs re:IsSpellEffect(), the literal passcode 78193831 instead of the named CARD_BUSTER_BLADER constant) are upstream idiom.
